title: QBR - Harbor Data health check
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage trends, cost drivers, recent reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment for next quarter. Agreement to run a dedicated performance benchmark on private deployment and to share granular cost report and SOC2/VPC docs.
topics: recent incident review and reliability metrics
action_items: Owner: Samantha Lee; Item: Share Q1 cost breakdown with per-route and per-model granularity; Due: 2026-04-02
Owner: Ivan Petrov; Item: Run 2-hour private deployment benchmark (latency & throughput) and send results; Due: 2026-04-08
Owner: Miguel Torres; Item: Send SOC2 documentation, VPC on-boarding checklist, and KMS integration guide; Due: 2026-04-05
Owner: Priya Singh; Item: Confirm internal stakeholders and preferred pilot cluster size; Due: 2026-04-06
next_steps: Redwood to send detailed cost and usage report
Schedule 2-hour dedicated benchmark window on Harbor staging VPC
Share security/compliance artifacts and start legal SOW discussion if benchmark looks good
Follow-up meeting in 2 weeks to review benchmark and finalize pilot scope
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Time: 14:00 - 14:45 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood CSM), Ivan Petrov (Redwood SE); Kevin Moore (Harbor Data), Priya Singh (Harbor Data), Liam Chen (Harbor Data)

[00:00] Samantha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick QBR for Harbor Data — we wanted to cover usage trends, cost, reliability incidents from last month, and then talk about next quarter roadmap. mic check?
[00:18] Kevin (Harbor): Yep, we can hear you. thanks, Sam.
[00:22] Priya (Harbor): Morning all, hi.
[00:26] Miguel (Redwood CSM): Morning! I'll take notes on action items.

[00:30] Samantha: Great. Quick agenda: 1) usage and cost, 2) reliability incidents and fixes, 3) roadmap alignment and pilot ask, 4) security docs and next steps. Does that work?
[00:40] Priya: Yep. can we make sure we have time for the private deployment discussion? That's our main ask.
[00:46] Samantha: Yes absolutely. Ivan, do you want to walk through the usage/cost deck?

[00:52] Ivan (Redwood SE): Sure. I'll share screen after, but high level — Harbor's token usage ramped 38% month over month in March mainly from the new summarization pipeline. Most of the traffic is short chat-ish requests but with occasional long-context runs for batch summarization. That drives token variance.
[01:15] Liam (Harbor): yeah those long-run jobs are our batch nightly summarization — they spike around 02:00 UTC and sometimes we see increased latency.
[01:23] Ivan: Right. And on cost side, our report shows 62% of spend tied to the long-context summarization jobs because of seq length and model selection (we're routing to a higher-capacity model for quality).

[01:40] Samantha: To be clear, the two levers are: change routing policy to a cheaper model for some of the batch runs, or tune quantization/kv cache to reduce per-token cost. Redwood Optimize recommendations are in the report.
[01:55] Kevin: We're concerned about quality drop if we change models. Some of the downstream QA folks noticed regressions when we tried the lighter model last quarter.
[02:04] Ivan: Totally, we saw that in the PoC. The suggestion is canary the cheaper model for 10% of jobs first and measure ROUGE/QA diffs. we can also keep the heavy model for any flagged workflows.
[02:17] Priya: That sounds sensible. what's the expected unit cost delta?
[02:21] Ivan: For the workloads you shared, switching to the quantized variant and toggling batching pairs reduces per-token spend by roughly 30% on those nightly jobs. The canary experiment should give you exact numbers.

[02:40] Miguel: quick note — there are also caching wins. since the nightly runs share many prefixes, enabling prefix/KV cache aggressively reduces repeated decoding. we've seen 15-25% token savings in similar setups.
[02:54] Liam: okay that's interesting, can we enable that on staging?

[03:00] Ivan: Yes, we can enable on your staging cluster, but note the caching behavior depends on model variant and max seq length. We'll configure and show the expected savings in the benchmark.

[03:15] Samantha: Next, reliability. Kevin, do you want to recap the incident on March 12?
[03:21] Kevin: Sure. At 02:10 UTC we had a region-level capacity shortage; requests hit timeouts for ~18 minutes. Our fallbacks routed to the hosted tier but we saw increased latency and several failed webhook deliveries.
[03:36] Miguel: Right, the routing policy was triggered. We had auto-fallback to Redwood Hosted which kept things up but with higher p95 from 220ms to 720ms for short chat routes.
[03:49] Priya: The business impact was some delayed customer notifications; we logged ~120 failed webhooks that retried and eventually delivered, but it caused alert storms.
[03:58] Ivan: On our side we captured the scheduler metrics — we hit a capacity cliff because of concurrent long-context jobs occupying GPU slots. we've got two mitigations: smarter routing by request priority and dedicated reserved capacity for the batch window.
[04:13] Samantha: That leads us to Dedicated / Private options. Priya, you mentioned interest in Private (VPC/on-prem) for compliance and control?
[04:22] Priya: Yes — SOC2 and data residency are a must for us next year. We also want better predictability for these nightly jobs. Dedicated capacity with a reserved pool sounds attractive.
[04:33] Kevin: Also want encryption with our KMS and SSO/SAML integration. We can't have logs leaving our VPC without controls.
[04:41] Miguel: Understood. Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC and KMS integrations; we can also offer an on-prem package if needed. We'll share the VPC checklist and KMS guide.

[04:55] Ivan: For Dedicated sizing, you run a 3-hour nightly job with spikes to ~120 concurrent streams at peak. For one-to-one parity with current performance you'd need roughly X GPUs (we'll provide exact counts in the benchmark plan). The dedicated pool can be configured to scale for burst windows.
[05:14] Priya: What's the SLA for Dedicated? We need p99 latency targets for short chat routes.
[05:20] Samantha: Our Dedicated contracts include an SLA for uptime and an SLO for p99 tail latencies with credits for breach. We'll send the SLA appendix.

[05:30] Liam: On security, are audit logs available per request? We need per-token traceability for compliance audits.
[05:36] Miguel: Yes, audit logs and request tracing are available; you can push logs to your cloud logging endpoint or we can provide a push/pull feed for retention. Red- word — sometimes the transcriber misspells product names — but the feature is there.
[05:49] Kevin: haha noted.

[05:53] Samantha: Let's talk about the benchmark. Ivan, propose the scope and we can lock a window.
[05:58] Ivan: Proposal: 2-hour benchmark on your staging VPC, replicate peak nightly workload including long-context summarization. We'll run the following: 1) Current hosted config baseline, 2) Dedicated pool with same model/quant, 3) Dedicated with quantized model + caching, 4) Private (VPC) with KMS enabled to validate end-to-end. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, throughput, and cost per 1M tokens.
[06:25] Priya: That works. We can grant temporary access to staging. prefer next week Wed/Thu after 10:00 UTC.
[06:33] Ivan: I'll put proposed slots. We'll need a small SRE contact from Harbor for access setup — Liam?
[06:38] Liam: Yep I can handle that.

[06:42] Miguel: On the cost reconciliation — Samantha will share the per-route, per-model cost breakdown and an Optimize report highlighting expected wins.
[06:50] Samantha: Yep. Expect the report today or tomorrow. It includes recommendations: caching, batching, canary plan, and quantization suggestions.

[07:00] Kevin: Quick question on latency tradeoffs: if we quantize for nightly, would inference throughput increase but p99 for short chat degrade?
[07:08] Ivan: Good question. Typically quantization reduces memory and increases throughput but can increase CPU overhead for some kernels; for short chat routes (low seq) we've seen neutral to slightly better p95, but p99 depends on tail scheduling. That's why the benchmark will measure both short and long routes.

[07:26] Priya: Anything on pricing models for Dedicated — is it pure committed monthly or flexible?
[07:31] Samantha: We offer reserved capacity contracts (monthly/annual commits) with burst options. There's also hybrid where you use Hosted for some traffic and Dedicated for reserved recurring workload. We'll include pricing scenarios in the cost deck.

[07:43] Kevin: Competitor note — our infra folks also evaluated Vertex AI and Replicate; Replicate was cheaper but had reliability gaps for long-context models. we picked Redwood for the routing and ops features.
[07:57] Miguel: Helpful context, thanks.

[08:02] Samantha: Okay let's surface the recap and actions. Recap: 1) Redwood to send cost/usage report and SLA appendix. 2) Run 2-hour benchmark on Harbor staging (Ivan to run, Liam to provide access). 3) Share SOC2 and VPC/KMS docs (Miguel). 4) Follow-up meeting in ~2 weeks to review results and finalize pilot.
[08:24] Priya: Sounds good. One more thing — can we get a sample SOW for Dedicated so procurement can start reviewing?
[08:30] Samantha: Yes we'll send a sample SOW and procurement checklist.

[08:35] Kevin: Great, appreciate it.
[08:38] Miguel: I'll capture the action items and drive the docs share.

[08:43] Samantha: Thanks everyone. we'll send notes and put next steps in calendar.
[08:47] Priya: Thanks all.
[08:49] Liam: Thanks.

[08:52] End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings for product names (Redwood Optimize sometimes transcribed as 'red would optimize' in automated text), and some timestamps approximate.
